related_questions.question: What is the inflation rate in Zimbabwe?

text_blocks.snippet: Zimbabwe has been grappling with high inflation rates for years. While the exact current rate varies depending on the source and time period, recent reports indicate a significant slowing of inflation, particularly on a month-on-month basis, with the June 2025 monthly rate at 0.3%. However, the annual rate remains elevated, though it has also shown signs of slowing down.

list.title: June 2025 Monthly Inflation:
list.snippet: The Zimbabwe Statistics Agency (ZimStat) reported a monthly inflation rate of 0.3% in June 2025, a decrease from the 0.9% recorded in May, according to deVere Zimbabwe.

list.title: Annual Inflation:
list.snippet: While the monthly rate has decreased, the annual inflation rate, which compares prices to the same month in the previous year, is still elevated, though the exact figure is not consistently reported in the provided search results. The World Economic Forum reports that annual inflation was at 55.3% in March 2024, which was a seven-month high at the time.

list.title: Historical Context:
list.snippet: Zimbabwe has a history of high inflation, including hyperinflation in the past, with rates exceeding 500% in recent years. In 2020, the annual inflation rate was reported as 557.2%, according to Statista.

list.title: Currency Changes:
list.snippet: Zimbabwe has recently introduced a new currency, the Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG), to address the persistent inflation issues and promote stability. The ZiG is intended to circulate alongside other foreign currencies.

list.title: Factors Contributing to Inflation:
list.snippet: The weakening of the Zimbabwean dollar against other currencies is cited as a contributing factor to rising inflation. Additionally, the use of US dollars in the economy has led to adjustments in the way inflation is measured to better reflect the reality of price increases.
